title: A Claude Team is declared by a profile: wb init sets up its board, hv is reached through one node, and the fleet converges
objective:
A project's Claude Team is declared once, by naming a profile, and the tool does the rest: `intent wb init <profile>` registers every seat with its canonical name, role and remit, the board says who reaches hv, and a session that boots on that board is told its own seat without hv typing it. This is hv's ask of 2026-11-10, relayed by the vc of a swarm hv had just started and ruled in vc's session the same day. hv was writing the same roster brief by hand at the start of every swarm, and the fleet's boards show what that has cost.

Concretely:

1. The terms are defined once, in Intent: Claude Team, Claude Swarm, Team Profile, the seats with their monikers, names and roles, the mediator, and the hat (WP-01).
2. A Team Profile is a shipped Intent resource of config and prose. `team` declares vc, cc, ic, ac, dc and hv; `solo` declares gc and hv; `supervisor` and `supervised` add the cross-project layer (WP-02).
3. `intent wb init <profile>` reconciles a board to its profile. It is a dry run by default; it registers what is missing, corrects what drifted and leaves everything else on the board alone; and running it again is the reinit (WP-03). A seat can be retired, and a board can change its profile (WP-04).
4. hv is reached through one node, and the tool enforces it: hv's only inbox pair is with the mediator, an ask to hv from any other node is refused with the mediator named, and an announce no longer copies hv (WP-05).
5. A session reads its brief at pickup: its seat, its remit, the route to hv and the hats it wears (WP-06). The roster README is rendered from the profile and keeps a block that is the project's own (WP-07).
6. The Desk is a hat with a written contract, worn by one VC on a host (WP-08).
7. Doctor reports a board that has left its profile (WP-09), the surface reads as one (WP-10), and every live board on this machine is converged, Intent's own first (WP-11).
context:
**Why.** hv, 2026-11-10, to the vc of a swarm hv had just started on a client project: "I seem to have to write this same message every time I start a new Claude Swarm, which is a bit frustrating." The message is the roster and its mandates: who the nodes are, what each is for, and how hv is reached. Nothing in Intent holds it. `intent wb register` takes one node at a time, with a name and a role typed by hand; the roster README is hand-authored and has no single writer; and a pickup reads neither. hv's shape for the fix, in the same message: "A profile should be an Intent resource that is just some simple config plus possibly some text that we can give to the LLM on init to set up the whiteboard", and "This needs to work with the existing "intent wb register..." workflow, too."

**What was measured, read-only, on 2026-11-10.** vc read every live whiteboard on rhadamanth: 32 boards (18 under `~/Devel/prj`, 3 under `prj/Arca`, 9 in a client tree and 2 under `~/Devel/writing`), holding 130 node rows.

- 38 rows carry their moniker as their role and 26 carry a session name as their display name. `intent wb register --help` warns against both.
- One moniker has several role words. `dc` is `dc` on 13 boards, `devx` on 7 and `worker` on 3, Intent's own among them. `ac` is `ac` on 5, `authoring` on 2 and `author` on 1. `hv` is `hypervisor` on all 24 boards that have it.
- The 32 boards hold 17 different rosters. 3 hold all five of vc, cc, ic, ac and dc. 8 have no `hv` node, so no escalation surface, and 6 have no roster README, so no named reader of hv's inbox.
- 10 boards carry a Supervisor Claude: `sc` on a hub's own board in 3, and `sv`, the supervisor's seat on a supervised project's board, in 7.
- 884 board messages have been addressed to hv, and 741 of them are copies of an `announce` (883 and 740 at vc's first reading half an hour earlier, the figures hv's question quoted). hv has sent 5. 112 inbox views pair hv with a node that does not mediate, and 100 of those are empty.
- `intent claude start` registers nothing: it reads the node and refuses an absent one. `intent wb register <moniker>` refuses without `--name` and `--role`. So the drifted rows were typed or migrated, and no launcher wrote them.
- The Desk's duties are written in one place, `lib/templates/estate/_AGENTS.md`, for a dedicated coordinator that stands in no project. No skill names the desk, so each VC that has worn it learned it from hv's prose.

The instrument and its output are banked as refs/bank/vc/st0092/census-boards.zsh (a651ef150413) and refs/bank/vc/st0092/census-20261110.txt (cf5d0de46fd7), read at 08:29Z by `date -u`.

**hv's rulings, 2026-11-10.** Seven by selection in the TUI hv asked for, each of them vc's recommendation; the first four were answered between 08:07Z and 08:11Z and the last three by 08:13Z, on vc's `date -u`. The wording is vc's and each choice is hv's.

1. A Claude Team is the standing roster a profile registers on a project's board, every member registered whether started or not. A Claude Swarm is whichever of a Team's sessions are running at one time.
2. The Supervisor has its own profile, shipped in this thread. hv, in prose the same hour: "SC is only needed on larger projects where we need multi-project coordination that goes across multiple VCs. Its not needed for a single swarm/tean."
3. The single Claude is `gc`, Generalist Claude, role `generalist`.
4. Sleeve agents and estate agents stay out of the profile mechanism. The terms name them, with Molt and Gtools as their owners.
5. hv's mediation is enforced by the tool.
6. The roster README is generated, with a preserved block.
7. The sweep writes directly where a project has no running session and through its vc or sc where one is running: all 32 boards, Intent's own first.

And hv's prose in vc's session, the same morning:

- The default Team: "a Claude Swarm (or Team) has, by default: VC, CC, IC, AC, and DC. The fact that not all of the Team is started at any one time is just a detail of use, they all should be registered and ready to be used if needed. If there is a case where just need 1 Claude and not a swarm, then that should be a different profile with a differnt role, abbreviation, and remit."
- The terms: "we canonically define the terms: Claude Swarm vs Claude Team; the correct abbreviations CC vs Control, etc; and the same definitions in each case for what the roles do."
- hv's own role: "We need to tidy up the HV / Hypervisor role and actions. It's ad-hoc right now, and needs to be made explicit. If you look at how the projects work, HV interactions are (or shouild be!) mediated thru the VC. Having HV detritous in the other Claude's inbox/whiteboards is a distraction at best, and intellectual pollution at worst."
- The sweep: "When done, we do an estate sweep and reach in thru each project's spinal cord and just do some brain surgery so that they are in line with this profile based approach."
- Pipeliner's `sc`: "I think that was a mistake and probably needs to be revoked and just back to a normal VC/CC/IC/DC/AC mix."
- The Desk: "The way I have been using this is as an extra "hat" that one VC wears. That _seems_ to be working, but we need to institutionalise the way that role works in addition to the other VC roles."

The seat names are hv's of 2026-10-21, recorded until now in Molt's roster README and nowhere in Intent.

**What this thread does not do.**

- It ships no user-authored profile. `intent ext` is declared and not built, and nothing reads `~/.local/share/intent/ext/`. A profile is Intent's canon, the same on every machine that runs the same Intent.
- It gives no sleeve agent or estate agent a profile or a board, and it installs Intent in no project that lacks it (hv, 2026-09-23).
- It does not fix issue 0672. It carries that issue's lesson as AC-07.4: a generated contract states what was declared, and never a default guessed for the project.
- It renames no node. A seat that must change its moniker is retired and its successor registered.

**Order and release.** WP-01 lands first, and no code is written before hv has ratified its document (AC-01.5). WP-02 and WP-03 follow in that order, and WP-04 to WP-09 stand on them. WP-11 runs only once the brew-installed Intent on this machine carries WP-02 to WP-10. The thread adds verbs. Which release carries it, and where it sits against the held 3.2.9 train, is hv's to say.

**Builders and judge.** cc builds WP-02 to WP-09 and ic builds WP-10, each claiming its package in the chain that starts it. vc writes WP-01 under hv's pen and directs WP-11. vc judges every bank and claims nothing, and each builder mints its package's AT rows with its bank. These assignments are vc's proposal, for hv's review of this elaboration.

wps.title: The terms are defined once: Team, Swarm, profile, the seats, the mediator and the hat
wps.objective: Intent holds one document that defines the words this thread uses and every project's board will use: Claude Team, Claude Swarm, Team Profile, node, moniker, name, role, session name, mediator and hat, with each seat's moniker, name, role and default remit, and hv's own contract. Everything else cites it. It is written and ratified before any code, because every later package renders or enforces what it says.
wps.body:
## Builder and judge

vc writes this package under hv's pen: its content is hv's rulings of 2026-11-10 and hv's seat names of 2026-10-21, written down. It is written in cc's tree, and cc reads it when it starts WP-02. The judge is `critic-prose` on the document, `prettier --check`, and hv's own read, which AC-01.5 records. vc claims nothing.

## What is written

One hand-authored document in the plugin canon, `intent/plugins/claude/teams/TERMS.md`, registered in `intent/llm/MODULES.md` before it was created. It ships with the install, so a session in any project can be shown it, and WP-02 adds the verb that prints it. It carries no frontmatter, as its neighbours under `rules/_schema` carry none, and it names no command, because the verbs that will print and apply it are not built. `intent/docs/working-with-llms.md` links to it and restates none of it.

It holds, in this order: the whiteboard, the board and the seat, with the seat's four labels, its remit, and registered, started and running; Team, Swarm and Profile, with base and layer and the four shipped profiles; the seats table; the mediator; hv's part and how every seat works with hv; the hat and the Desk; and the two kinds of Claude that hold no seat. The wording is the document's, and this package does not restate it.

## What it is not

It is not the protocol: the `/in-whiteboard` skill keeps that and cites this document for the words. It is not the source of the seat rows once WP-02 lands: from then the shipped profiles are, and AC-02.5 fails a build in which the document's table and the profiles disagree.

## The critic's read, 2026-11-10

`critic-prose` read the first draft (f6e987017) with the author pack: no critical finding, the mechanical tier clean, and eight craft warnings, most of them one word carrying two senses. Its verdict was that the draft was close and not yet fit for ratification. vc applied all eight in the document's wording, with no ruling's meaning changed:

- A project's **whiteboard** and a seat's **board** are now two words. The draft used board for both.
- The four things that go with a seat are its labels, so that name means the display name alone.
- A Team "exists whether or not any session is running", where the draft's "while no session is running" read as only then.
- The mediator is named by the base profile, and the `supervisor` layer moves it to sc. The draft's three cases overlapped, because a hub is also a `team` whiteboard.
- A supervisor "is not needed for one Team on its own", which is hv's verb.
- A seat that hv rules to directly passes the ruling to the mediator, so who puts a matter to hv has one answer.
- The sentence that every seat is a project's own is gone: sv and hv are seats and neither is.
- Monikers are lower-case throughout.

## For hv's eye at ratification

Twelve points are before hv, each with vc's recommendation. Nine were put on 2026-11-10 before any seat had read the document, and three came from cc's read of it against Intent's own board the same day. The first six are vc's wordings where hv's rulings left room, and vc recommends each as written:

1. Only the mediator puts options to hv, and hv may speak to any seat directly. That is the strict reading of "mediated thru the VC".
2. "No seat waits idle on hv. A seat that needs a ruling asks the mediator, holds only the work that depends on the answer, and carries on with the rest." The ruling's own words were that nobody waits on hv, which a literal reader could take as leave to go on without the ruling.
3. On a hub the `supervisor` layer makes sc the mediator, and vc's default remit still ends "and the one route to hv". vc recommends leaving the default and letting a hub set its own vc remit.
4. "sequencing" is in both vc's default remit and hv's, in hv's own words for each.
5. The default remits of gc, sc and sv are vc's, and so is ac's "Authoring and content creation".
6. `team` is called the standard Team and not the default, so that a whiteboard that declares nothing is not read as a `team` whiteboard.

The next three come from the spike, and vc recommends adding each:

7. cc's default remit. hv's words are "Back-end services and the non-user-facing implementation of services". A project that is still modelling has no service, so read literally the remit gives cc none of the work there is, and no seat owns the data model. Proposed: "The core: the model, its rules, and the back-end services that implement them, in whatever form they take at the time, documents and data included."
8. The boundary between cc and ic on a contract. ic holds machine-facing interfaces and cc the implementation behind them, so nobody owns the contract itself. Proposed, one sentence after the seats table: "Where an interface has a contract, cc is authoritative on what it means and ic on its shape and transport, and a change to it needs both."
9. A path for disagreement with the mediator. The mediator is the one filter, and on the spike's board it was the source of three errors in one day, each caught by hv or by the seat that had reported the matter and never by the structure. Proposed, one line in hv's section: "A seat that disagrees with what the mediator has put to hv says so to the mediator, and the mediator puts the disagreement to hv in the seat's own words."

The last three are cc's, from reading the document against Intent's own board, and vc recommends each:

10. The pen. The document says the mediator "presents a matter for hv's review and does not decide it". hv's decision of 2026-08-22 on Intent's board gives vc the pen, and vc rules under it daily, each ruling recorded as vc's and open to hv's reversal. cc's words: "on Intent's board its own mediator breaks the sentence that defines it". cc proposes naming the pen as a second hat, whose scope is one whiteboard, worn by the mediator on hv's word, with each ruling under it recorded as the wearer's and "does not decide" narrowed to what hv keeps. The other course is to withdraw the pen where a board converges. The point concerns vc's own authority, so vc's recommendation, the hat, is an interested one and hv weighs it as that.
11. "Solo" is already used. `.claude/restart.md` called a session that holds no seat solo, and the shipped finish skill calls a project with one workstream solo, while the document makes `solo` the profile of one Claude and hv. Proposed: the profile keeps its name, the document defines the session that holds no seat under its own word, an unseated session, beside the sleeve and estate agents, and the two older lines are reworded. Intent's own was reworded on 2026-11-10.
12. The human seat has no session. "Registered, started, running" are defined for every seat, and a seat is read as never started from the absence of a recorded session, so every board would print hv as never started. Proposed, one sentence: the three states belong to a seat a session drives, and hv's seat is only ever registered.

Two wording fixes go in with the ratification unless hv objects, both cc's. The session name is the project's name in lower case with the moniker, since the project is `Intent` and its sessions are `intent-cc`. And the Desk's scope covers a machine that books its runs on another host's desk, as a guest VM does.

hv ratified the document on 2026-11-10, first-hand in vc's session, read at 19:26:54Z on vc's `date -u`, in these words: "Ratified as recommended". That takes all twelve points as vc recommended them and both wording fixes. vc edited the document to it the same day: points 1 to 6 stand as written, and points 7 to 12 and the two fixes are now in it. The pen of point 10 is defined as a hat whose scope is one whiteboard, and it does not reach scope, release policy, the ratification of a decision, or anything hv has said is hv's alone.

## Depends on

Nothing. Every other package waits on AC-01.5.

wps.title: A Team Profile is a shipped resource: team, solo, supervisor and supervised
wps.objective: The four profiles ship in Intent's plugin canon as files of config and prose under one schema, and the installed tool lists, shows and validates them the way it serves the rule library. No project vendors a profile, so a project names one and never copies it.
wps.body:
## Builder and judge

cc builds this package and claims `ST0092/02` in the same chain as `intent wp start ST0092/02`, once AC-01.5 is recorded. vc judges it and claims nothing.

## What is built

- **The seat registry**, one JSON file beside `TERMS.md` in the plugin canon under `intent/plugins/claude/`, read by a typed, strict reader. It holds each seat once: its moniker, its name, its role, who drives it and its default remit. hv's row is written once, and a moniker cannot carry two names.
- **The profile files**, beside the registry, one `.md` per profile. The frontmatter is flat: the profile's kind (a base or a layer), the mediator it sets, and the monikers of its seats. The body is the brief, the prose a session is given: what the team is, how hv is reached, what each seat owes the others, and what a seat does at launch. A base's body carries four sections that are printed whole and stated nowhere else: the route to hv and the launch steps, each written once for the mediator and once for every other seat. The pickup's brief, the launcher and the roster README choose between the two by whether the seat is the declared mediator (WP-06, WP-07). The sections name the mediator from the board's declaration and never as a moniker written into the prose, because a layer can move it. A layer's body carries none of the four: it is the layer's own prose, printed after the base's, so a board that declares a base and a layer has one source for each section.
- **The four profiles.** `team` is a base: vc, cc, ic, ac, dc and hv, with vc the mediator. `solo` is a base: gc and hv, with gc the mediator. `supervisor` is a layer for a hub: it adds sc and makes sc the mediator. `supervised` is a layer for a project under a supervisor: it adds sv and leaves the mediator alone.
- **A schema** for the registry and one for the profile file, beside the rule schema, and a loader in the library crate (`native/rust/crates/intentsvcs/`) whose every failure is a typed error with a remedy.
- **Four read-only verbs**, `intent wb profile list`, `intent wb profile show <name>`, `intent wb profile validate` and `intent wb profile terms`, which prints WP-01's document. The dispatch is in `intent-cli` and the logic in the library. They answer from the install and need no project.
- **Validation** refuses a base with no mediator, a mediator that is not one of the profile's seats, a duplicate moniker, a role equal to its moniker, a name written as a session name, a second seat driven by the human, a layer that declares a human seat, a profile that names a moniker the registry does not hold, a base that lacks any of its four sections, and a layer that carries one.
- **The parity test** of AC-02.5, which reads the seats table in the terms document and the seat registry and fails on any difference in moniker, name, role, driver or default remit.
- **The surface rows** for the four verbs in `surface/dispatch-table.json`, which ic reads as the table's owner before the bank is judged.

`intent/llm/MODULES.md` gains each new module's row before the module is created.

## vc's ruling on the design

On 2026-11-10 cc proposed the registry in its design notes, and vc took it under hv's pen. A seat written into each profile that uses it gives hv's row two homes, in `team` and in `solo`, and gives the parity test two tables to hold against the terms. The registry gives each seat one. The file's format is cc's to choose, within what the workspace already parses.

cc then read the package as its builder and could not build the brief as written, and vc ruled again the same day. The mediator's route and launch step differ from every other seat's, so each is written twice, and the reader chooses. And a board can declare a base and a layer, so only the base carries the four sections.

## What it must not do

It reads nothing from `~/.local/share/intent/ext/` and vendors nothing into a project. A user-authored profile is out of this thread.

## The judge

One heavy run on the bank's tip, booked with the estate's controller: the workspace's whole test suites and the whole shell suite, `intent critic rust --files` on each changed Rust file (vc decision 79), `prettier --check` on each changed Markdown file, and `bin/int precommit` over the staged tree. cc mints this package's AT rows with its bank, and each arm carries its AT id from the start.

## Rulings since this package was written, 2026-11-10

These are vc's rulings under the pen, made on ic's read of the dispatch rows and cc's read as builder, and written here once hv ratified the terms. Where one disagrees with the text above, it stands and the text above gives way.

The four `wb profile` verbs are reads, offered on MCP, and their help says they answer from the installed Intent and need no project, with an arm run outside any project. `validate` exits 0 when every profile is valid, 1 on a finding or a refusal, and 2 when the build cannot answer. An unknown profile is a typed refusal on exit 1 (INV-04) naming the shipped profiles. `terms` reads no profile, and its help says it prints the document every profile shares.

## Depends on

WP-01, ratified.

wps.title: wb init reconciles a board to its profile, and is a dry run until told to apply
wps.objective: `intent wb init <profile>` brings a board to what its profiles declare and touches nothing else on it. Without `--apply` it writes nothing and says what it would do. It works where a project has no whiteboard yet and on a board that has been live for months, and running it again is the reinit hv asked for.
wps.body:
## Builder and judge

cc builds this package and claims `ST0092/03` in the same chain as `intent wp start ST0092/03`. vc judges it and claims nothing.

## What is built

- **`intent wb init <base> [<layer>...] [--apply]`**, in the facade, as a coordinator over the identity door that already exists. For each seat the profiles declare it registers an absent one (`wb_register`), corrects a name or role that differs (`wb_correct`) and leaves a matching one alone. A registered node that no profile names is reported as outside the profile and left as it is. It is the third way onto the roster beside the two `intent wb register` has: one node from its arguments, and every node from its own board header.
- **The declaration.** The board's base, its layers, its mediator and its human seat are recorded in the store and as canon on disk under `intent/whiteboard/`, so a clone ingests the same team. The declared human seat is where every reader takes a seat's driver from: that seat is the human's, and every other seat is a session's, one that no profile names included. The same file holds the roster README's baseline, the hash each render of it records (WP-07). The canon is one file, rendered from the store as a `board.json` is and never edited by hand, and `intent doctor` reports skew in it. `intent wb init --apply` with no profile named re-applies the declaration: that is the reinit.
- **The remit.** The node row gains a remit, on the seat's own row and nowhere else, and it holds only a remit the project set. An apply writes no remit. `intent wb remit <moniker> "<text>"` sets a project's own and re-renders the roster README, and `intent wb remit <moniker> --default` removes it. A seat with none shows its profile's default wherever a remit is shown, read from the installed profile at that moment and marked as the default. So a row never has to say where its remit came from, and a default that a later release rewords reaches every project that kept it, with no apply. The dry run names every seat whose remit would be the profile's default, because no board has a stored remit today and 26 state their own in README prose. The first swarm set up by hand found on 2026-11-10 that a first apply would state each remit twice and differently, and that its own wording for cc is narrower than the default in the way that separates cc from ic on its board.
- **`register` honours the declaration.** A moniker the declared profiles name registers only with the profile's name and role, and the refusal prints them. A moniker they do not name registers as it does today. This is what stops the drift where it starts: 38 of 130 rows fleet-wide carry a role typed in as the moniker.
- **The dry run.** For each seat one of `register`, `correct` with the old and the new value, `unchanged` or `outside the profile`, then every view it would write or remove.
- **The apply's report.** Every path on a `wrote:` or `removed:` line, and one line saying that this is the roster's own mechanical commit, the carve-out in the protocol's ninth invariant, made by the coordinating node or hv. The vc that relayed hv's ask measured the reach by hand on 2026-11-10: registering `hv` wrote ten files across four boards.
- **The refusals**, each a typed error with a remedy: a hand-authored node that has not been migrated (`intent wb migrate`); a base other than the one declared (`--change`, WP-04); an unknown profile, with the shipped names; a layer on a board with no base.
- **The schema.** `board.json` moves on from `intent/board@4.0` for the new fields. A build of this thread reads a board at 4.0 unchanged. The new shape is not bent to stay readable by 3.2.8, whose `Board` and `WbNode` refuse an unknown field (vc's ruling of 2026-11-10 on cc's design note).
- **The surface rows** for `wb init` and `wb remit`, read by ic.

## What it never touches

Items, messages, handled marks, claims, archives, heartbeats, status and focus. AC-03.3 compares the bytes.

## Risks

- An apply is many roster writes at once, and a running intentd ingests disk over store after a quiet period (issue 0216). The apply is one store transaction and one landing of views, and its test reads the result back after the ingest.
- A registration re-renders every other board's inbox set, so the apply's file list is long on a large team. It is printed whole.
- An Intent that predates the new schema will meet these boards on any machine that has not upgraded. WP-11 measures what the released Intent does with one before any project is converged.
- A build of this thread moves a project's store forward the first time it opens it, by a read or a dry run as much as by an apply, and every older reader of that store is then refused (cc's measurement of 2026-11-10: the migration runs in `Store::open`). So until the cut, this package and every one after it is driven on a clone of Intent's board, and never on the real one while a 3.2.8 session reads it.

## Rulings since this package was written, 2026-11-10

These are vc's rulings under the pen, made on ic's read of the dispatch rows and cc's read as builder, and written here once hv ratified the terms. Where one disagrees with the text above, it stands and the text above gives way.

Without `--apply`, `wb init` writes no tracked file and no board row. The help says a store this build has not opened is upgraded at that first open, as by any verb, and AC-03.2's arm asserts the tracked tree unchanged by hash. The upgrade note lives once, in the CHANGELOG and the guide. The dry run exits 0. `wb init` is CLI only as a roster act, with the reason in `recoverability_anomaly`. `--change` takes its own flag disposition, because it retires seats. More refusals: the reinit (`--apply` with no profile) on a board with no recorded declaration, naming the shipped profiles; WP-05's live hv inbox; and WP-07's three README refusals. The roster-commit line is a `note:`. `wb remit` refuses both `<text>` and `--default`, and refuses neither; it is reversible and CLI only. The help for `wb register`'s `--name` and `--role` says a declared moniker takes the profile's values. The apply is one `wb_write_then_record` with one `wb.init` event and one landing, over refusal checks lifted out of `wb_register` and `wb_correct`. AC-03.9 lands green with its note.

## Rulings on the second row read, 2026-11-10

These are vc's rulings under the pen on ic's read of this package against the dispatch table at d6f56d7e6. Where one disagrees with anything above, the section before it included, it stands and the text above gives way.

`wb init` takes one positional, `profile`, arity 0..n. The library classifies each name by the kind its shipped profile declares, base or layer, and every refusal is the library's: more than one base; a layer with no base, named or declared; a base that differs from the declared one without `--change`. The row is mutate, with `--apply` and `--change`, no `--node`, not on MCP, `recoverability: idempotent` with a `recoverability_anomaly` that points at `wb register`'s reason and does not restate it.

`wb remit` is a new row: mutate, arg `moniker` arity 1, arg `text` arity 0..1, flag `--default`, no `--node`, not on MCP, `recoverability: reversible` with the same pointing anomaly. `wb register` changes in help only, on `--name` and `--role`.

A dry run the apply would carry out exits 0. A dry run that meets a refusal prints it and exits 1, as the apply would (INV-04), and it reaches every refusal the apply would meet: an unmigrated node, an unknown profile, a live hv inbox, and WP-07's README refusals. The body and the help both say so. The roster-commit line is a `note:` (INV-01).

wps.title: A seat can be retired, and a board can change its profile
wps.objective: Intent has had no way to take a node off a roster, so a roster only grows. One supervisor hub's roster says so twice in prose and keeps a `vc` it calls paused and retired beside the `sc` that replaced it, and on 2026-11-10 the vc that relayed hv's ask registered four of the five seats hv declared and left `ac` out because a registration could not be undone. This package adds retirement as a state, never a deletion, and with it the move from one base profile to another, which is the other half of hv's reinit.
wps.body:
## Builder and judge

cc builds this package and claims `ST0092/04` in the same chain as `intent wp start ST0092/04`. vc judges it and claims nothing.

## What is built

- **`intent wb retire <moniker> --reason "<why>"`**, a roster act like `register`. Retired is a state on the roster, as archived is a state on a board. A retired node keeps its board, its items and every message it sent or received, all readable with `--all`. It is no longer a recipient: an ask to it is refused and names the retirement, and an announce skips it. `intent wb status` lists it only with `--all`, and a profile is reconciled against the roster without it.
- **Claims stop a retirement.** A node that holds a claim on a thread, a work package or an issue is refused, with each claim named: a node cannot take its claims with it.
- **Live messages do not stop it; they are reported.** A message the leaver sent stays in its recipient's inbox until the recipient handles it, and that pair's view is dropped only when it holds nothing live. A message addressed to the leaver that it never handled is named in the retirement's report and at its sender's next pickup, and the sender, who is that message's one writer, sends it on to another node or archives it: `intent wb archive message` no longer refuses when the recipient is retired. Nobody acts as the retired node.
- **The mediator is not retired** while it is the mediator. It goes only in a change of profile that names another.
- **Reinstatement** is `register` again: the same moniker comes back as the same node with its board, and a second node is never made.
- **`intent wb init <base> --change [--apply]`** moves a board from one base to another, eg from `solo` to `team` when a project grows. It registers the new base's seats and retires the seats of the old base that the new one does not declare, under the rules above, and its dry run lists both. It is the only way `wb init` retires anything: a plain re-apply reports a node outside the profile and leaves it.
- **The surface row** for `wb retire`, read by ic. vc's proposal for ic's row: a roster act is done because someone was asked, so it is not offered on MCP.

## Why retire and not rename

`register --correct` changes a node's name and role and keeps its moniker. A moniker is a routing key, a directory and a field in every message and event that names the node, so renaming one rewrites history across every board. Retiring the old seat and registering its successor changes no record: a hub's `vc` that became `sc`, and Riffle's and Prodinfra's `cc` if hv rules those boards solo at the sweep.

## Open for hv's review

These four are vc's design calls on the points the relaying vc raised on 2026-11-10, and each is cheap to change before the package is built: live messages are reported and do not refuse; claims refuse; a re-apply never retires without `--change`; and the verb is kept off MCP.

## Rulings since this package was written, 2026-11-10

These are vc's rulings under the pen, made on ic's read of the dispatch rows and cc's read as builder, and written here once hv ratified the terms. Where one disagrees with the text above, it stands and the text above gives way.

`wb retire` is reversible by `register`, CLI only, and `--reason` is required. An unknown moniker is a typed refusal on exit 1 naming the registered seats. The human seat is refused, because a human seat is only ever registered, as the terms say since hv ratified them. A seat already retired is a no-op that says so and exits 0. `wb status --all` is a new flag with its own row, MCP included. The help for `wb ask`, `wb announce` and `wb archive message` names the retired-node behaviour.

## Rulings on the second row read, 2026-11-10

These are vc's rulings under the pen on ic's read of this package against the dispatch table at d6f56d7e6. Where one disagrees with anything above, the section before it included, it stands and the text above gives way.

`wb retire` is a new row: mutate, arg `moniker` arity 1, `--reason` required, no `--node`, not on MCP. Its recoverability is `reversible`, with a `recoverability_anomaly` that points at `wb register`'s reason and does not restate it: a reversible act withheld from MCP because it decides who the participants are. An already retired seat is a no-op on exit 0 that says so on an `ok:` line.

`wb init` gains `--change`, not on MCP even if `wb init` is ever offered there, because it is the one path that retires seats. `wb status` gains `--all`, on MCP, help "include retired seats". `wb ask`, `wb announce` and `wb archive` change in help only.

`--all` keeps one meaning in the family: include what the default hides. That is handled messages on `wb show` and retired seats on `wb status`, and each help line names what it adds. `wb show <moniker>` of a retired seat answers without `--all`, and its header says retired.

wps.title: hv is reached through one node, and the tool enforces it
wps.objective: On a board that declares a profile, hv has one channel: with the mediator. The inbox pairs between hv and every other node stop being rendered, an ask to hv from any other node is refused with the mediator named, and an announce no longer copies hv. hv's directives, decisions and watch-outs still reach every node at pickup, because they are the team's law and not traffic.
wps.body:
## Builder and judge

cc builds this package and claims `ST0092/05` in the same chain as `intent wp start ST0092/05`. vc judges it and claims nothing.

## What was measured

Across the 32 live boards on 2026-11-10: 884 messages addressed to hv, of which 741 are copies of an `announce`; 5 messages sent by hv, ever; 112 inbox views pairing hv with a node that does not mediate, 100 of them empty. The cause is in the model: every registered node gets an inbox pair with every other, hv included, and an announce goes to every node but its sender.

The first swarm set up by hand, on 2026-11-10, showed what the convention this package replaces costs. Clearing hv's copy of an announce took two verbs, a clear as hv and an archive by its sender, because a clear marks a message handled and leaves the sender's rendered view as it was. Its vc then found itself sending a session message where an announce was right, to escape the cleanup. An announce must cost the mediator nothing, which AC-05.3 gives it.

## What is built

- **The pair.** The human seat has one inbox pair, with the mediator. No `<node>/inbox.hv.md` and no `hv/inbox.<node>.md` is rendered for any other node.
- **The ask.** `intent wb ask hv` from any other node is refused with a typed error whose remedy names the mediator and gives the same message as an ask to it. A message from the human seat to a node that is not the mediator is refused the same way: hv speaks to a node live, or the mediator carries it.
- **The announce** goes to every registered session node but the sender, and not to the human seat.
- **Writing as hv.** A write as the human seat from a Claude session bound to any node but the mediator is refused. The mediator's session writes hv's board under the pen, and a shell with no Claude session, which is hv's own terminal, writes it as before. The session's node is read from `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`, the identity the pickup already records. That read is one function, shared with WP-08's check of who may take the desk (vc's ruling of 2026-11-10 on cc's design note).
- **The standing items.** hv's directives, decisions and watch-outs print in full at every node's pickup, as they do now.
- **The crossing.** `intent wb init --apply` refuses to drop an hv inbox view that still holds a live message and names each one with its sender. The mediator surfaces them to hv and clears them as hv, and the apply then proceeds. Fleet-wide on 2026-11-10, 4 such messages come from a `dc` or a `cc`: 3 and 1. Every such message stays readable with `--all`. A message that is handled and not archived holds no view back: only a live one refuses.
- **Opt-in by declaration.** A board that declares no profile behaves exactly as it does today, so nothing changes for a project until its own `wb init`.
- **The skill.** `intent/plugins/claude/skills/in-whiteboard/SKILL.md` says what the tool now does, in the same landing: the hv section, the rule that the README must name hv's reader, which the profile's mediator replaces, and what `ask` and `announce` do.

## What a node loses, and does not

Nothing durable. An escalation that went to hv's inbox was read by nobody until the mediator ran, on every board whose README named one; it now goes to the mediator's inbox, which is read at the same moment. A node with a complaint about the mediator records it as a watch-out on its own board, which every pickup prints in full to every peer.

## Rulings since this package was written, 2026-11-10

These are vc's rulings under the pen, made on ic's read of the dispatch rows and cc's read as builder, and written here once hv ratified the terms. Where one disagrees with the text above, it stands and the text above gives way.

The hv-write check sits in the facade, the identity door, so MCP's node-taking writes meet it, and one arm drives an MCP write as hv from a non-mediator session. It is stated once, in the table's invariants. The help for `wb ask` and `wb announce` says "on a board that declares a profile".

## Rulings on the second row read, 2026-11-10

These are vc's rulings under the pen on ic's read of this package against the dispatch table at d6f56d7e6. Where one disagrees with anything above, the section before it included, it stands and the text above gives way.

The rule is the table's INV-12, carried in this package's bank with the facade check: "On a board that declares a profile, only the mediator's session or a shell with no session writes as the human seat". A write that takes `--node <human seat>` is refused unless the session it comes from is bound to the mediator, or no Claude session is present. The check sits in the facade, so the CLI and every MCP tool that takes a node meet the one check and no dispatch arm repeats it. The refusal is exit 1 with `error:`, and its remedy names the mediator. A board that declares no profile is unaffected.

The session-to-node read is one library function, `session_node`, with `mediator_of(board)` beside it. dc builds both in WP-08, and this package calls them and extends `mediator_of` to read a declared profile through `teams.rs`: the last layer that names a mediator wins, else the base's.

Twelve rows take `--node`, and seven of them are on MCP: archive, pickup, touch, release, claim, unclaim and clear. The MCP arm drives one of those seven. It also asserts that an MCP caller always carries a session id, since the server inherits `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` from the session that started it, so "no session" is never an MCP path.

No new row and no new flag. `wb ask`, `wb announce` and `wb init --apply` change in help and behaviour as the section above says.

wps.title: A session is told its seat at pickup and at launch
wps.objective: This is the package that ends the retyping. A session that boots on a profiled board reads, from the pickup alone, which team it is on, its own seat, name, role and remit, the node hv is reached through, the hats it wears, and every other seat with its remit, whether that seat has ever run or not.
wps.body:
## Builder and judge

cc builds this package and claims `ST0092/06` in the same chain as `intent wp start ST0092/06`. vc judges it and claims nothing. Issue 0675 is built with it, because both change what a pickup prints.

## What is built

- **The brief in `intent wb pickup`.** Ahead of the board it prints the declared profiles, this node's name, role and remit, the mediator, and one line for each other seat with its name, role, remit and whether it has ever run. `--json` carries the same fields. The MCP tool answers the same.
- **The mediator's own brief.** For the mediator the route is not a node to go through. Its brief says that it is the mediator, that it reaches hv directly, and that the other seats' requests for hv come to it.
- **A seat that has never run** is listed like any other and marked never started. hv, 2026-11-10: "they all should be registered and ready to be used if needed." The human seat carries no such mark, because no session drives it: the rule reads a seat's recorded session, hv's row never holds one, and so the exemption keys on the board's declared human seat (WP-03).
- **How old a read is**, which is issue 0675. `intent wb pickup` prints how long ago the acting node last picked up on this machine, and `intent wb status`, which has no acting node, prints the same age on the row of every seat a session drives. It is read from the store's own `wb.pickup` events, and a pickup reads it before it writes its own. Those events are machine-scoped and never reach canon, so a store ingested fresh from canon holds none: there the line says that no pickup of the node is recorded on this machine, and prints no age. One arm pins what a fresh clone prints. Each peer's line gives the number of live messages addressed to that peer, labelled live.
- **`intent wb brief <moniker>`**, a read that writes nothing: it prints a seat's brief, and with `--launch` its launch steps, and `--json` carries the same. The launcher is a script and the brief is computed in the library, so the launcher needs a door to it. That door cannot be a pickup, which moves the heartbeat and records a session: the launched session's own pickup must be the one that does both, under its own session id.
- **The launcher.** `intent claude start <node>` hands the session the same brief through `intent/plugins/claude/bin/intent_claude_cwi`, which composes the session's context today and takes the brief from `intent wb brief <node> --launch`. Its refusal of an unregistered moniker stays and now names `intent wb init`.
- **The launch steps come from the profile.** Today `compose_ctx` ends every launch on two steps written for a session that hv directs: show hv a detailed plan, then stop and wait for hv's instructions. On a board with a mediator that is wrong for every seat but one. The steps are the profile's (WP-02): a seat other than the mediator sends its plan to the mediator and takes its go from it, unless hv speaks to it directly, and the mediator shows its plan to hv. The launcher's opening line calls the session a seat, the terms' word, where today it says a workstream node. A board that declares no profile launches as it does today, with the two steps unchanged, because nothing changes for a project until its own `wb init` (WP-05).
- **The profile's prose** from WP-02 is what the brief prints after the seats: how hv is reached and what each seat owes the others. It is the one source of those words, for the pickup, the launcher and the roster README (WP-07).

## What the spike showed

On 2026-11-10 the first swarm set up by hand carried its brief as an hv standing directive, which today's pickup prints in full to every node. It reached every pickup, and it printed last, below the node's own items and live messages, where a 900-word message buried it. Ahead of the board is the requirement, as AC-06.1 says.

It also showed that `intent wb register` stamps a heartbeat at registration, so `intent wb status` prints a seat that has never run exactly as one that ran and paused. The row already holds the difference: no session has ever been recorded for it, and on the 32 live boards 4 session seats read that way that day. So never started is read from the absence of any recorded session, never from status or heartbeat, and the time a seat was registered is not printed as a heartbeat.

Its cold boot, the same day, was a partial pass. A seat that was registered and had never run was launched after the brief was in place. From its pickup alone it read its role, its remit, the mediator and the route to hv, and it followed the route without stating all of it. It did not get its own moniker from the pickup. Its start prompt named the seat, and no pickup can infer one, because the verb takes the moniker as an argument. So the launcher is the only source of the seat, and of this package's two halves the launcher's is the one the proof rests on. By the seat's own account the boot was not a clean one: its start prompt told it to run a pickup and read its inboxes, and hv typed to it while it booted, though neither named the role, the remit, the mediator or the route.

The remit reached that seat only inside the brief, because its own board holds a name and a role and no remit (AC-03.7). And the brief's line for it said registered and never started, which was false by the time the seat read it. So whether a seat has run is computed at the read and is never written into the brief's text.

## What the hand form showed

On 2026-11-10 Intent's own board was put into this thread's form by hand (d09791705): the brief as hv's directive 2, the roster README, and a "Your seat" section in `.claude/restart.md`. cc read it as this package's builder, and vc took its findings under hv's pen.

- The launcher's own steps contradicted the brief, and the hand form needed two patches over them: a paragraph of the directive, and the section in `.claude/restart.md`. That is why the launch steps come from the profile.
- The hand form handled the mediator with a special case in prose, "a seat other than vc". That is why the mediator has a brief of its own.
- The board became a control for the never-started mark. `ac`, registered that day and never launched, printed as paused with a heartbeat, and `hv`, which no session drives, printed as active with a heartbeat eight weeks old. Neither row holds a session.
- The route to hv was written by hand three times, in three wordings. The generated brief replaces all three, and WP-11 says how each hand copy is retired on Intent's own board.

## Why this and not the README

A pickup reads no README and never has (hv's decision 28, ruling 5, on Conflab). The README is for a person reading the repository; the pickup is what a session reads at every boot.

## The proof that matters

AC-06.4 is not a test. A session is launched with `intent claude start <node>` on a converged board and hv types nothing to it. vc records, by session id, that it stated its own seat, which the launcher gave it, and its role, its remit, the mediator and its route to hv, which its pickup gave it.

## Rulings since this package was written, 2026-11-10

These are vc's rulings under the pen, made on ic's read of the dispatch rows and cc's read as builder, and written here once hv ratified the terms. Where one disagrees with the text above, it stands and the text above gives way.

The facade returns one row per seat, which the CLI's `wb status`, its `--json` and MCP's `wb status` all render. It carries the live item count and the live message count, each labelled live, the last pickup stamp, the never-started mark (for session-driven seats only) and the desk hat (WP-08). MCP stops counting archived items and handled messages. `wb brief <moniker>` is a read, offered on MCP, with no `--node`, and the help for `--launch` says "prints the launch steps; launches nothing". Pickup's help, its `--json` and MCP carry the brief, with one arm comparing the three. The fresh-clone line is a `note:`, exit 0. `claude start`'s remedy names `wb init`.

## Rulings on the second row read, 2026-11-10

These are vc's rulings under the pen on ic's read of this package against the dispatch table at d6f56d7e6. Where one disagrees with anything above, the section before it included, it stands and the text above gives way.

`wb brief` is a new row: read, arg `moniker` arity 1, `--launch` (on MCP, help "prints the launch steps; launches nothing") and `--json` (not on MCP, with the family's terminal-channel note), no `--node`, on MCP.

Three edges of `wb brief`, each with an arm. On a board that declares no profile it answers on exit 0 with today's two steps and the node's name and role, and never refuses, so an unprofiled project's `claude start` is unchanged. For a retired seat it refuses on exit 1, naming the retirement with `wb register` as the remedy, and the launcher passes the refusal through. For the human seat, `--launch` refuses on exit 1 saying the seat is the human's, and without `--launch` it prints the seat's line. An unknown moniker refuses on exit 1 naming the registered seats.

The INV-09 arm covers four faces from one library function: pickup's prose, its `--json`, MCP's answer and `wb brief`. The fresh-clone line is a `note:`.

The launcher half is ic's, as a sub-unit of this package, and the script never calls `intent`. The door, `claude_cwi` in the CLI, fetches the brief through the facade, from the one function this package builds for `wb brief`, and hands the text to `intent/plugins/claude/bin/intent_claude_cwi` as an argument beside the display name. The script prints it with the restart context in place of the two hard-coded steps, and its opening line says seat. This replaces the route the text above names, a script calling `intent wb brief <node> --launch`: the binary on PATH may not be the one that resolved the project (issue 0609), and at the door the three edges are the facade's own typed refusals on exit 1 before any script runs. A board with no profile gets today's two steps from the same call. The unregistered-moniker remedy that names `wb init` is the library's `WbNodeNotRegistered` remedy, so it is cc's line and not the launcher's. ic builds its half once the brief function is banked. cc keeps the package's claim and builds the rest.

wps.title: The roster README is rendered from the profile and keeps the project's own block
wps.objective: `intent/whiteboard/README.md` becomes a generated view with one writer. `intent wb init --apply` renders its upper part from the declared profiles and the store, and everything below a marker is the project's own and survives every re-render. A profile change reaches a project at its next `wb init`, and a project loses none of what it wrote.
wps.body:
## Builder and judge

cc builds this package and claims `ST0092/07` in the same chain as `intent wp start ST0092/07`. vc judges it and claims nothing.

## What was measured

26 of the 32 live boards have a roster README and 6 have none. 5 carry a verblock. Intent's own says, in its own text, that it has no single writer and that its rows lag. The function that keeps a preserved block across a re-render already exists, `carry_user_block` in `native/rust/crates/intentsvcs/src/canon.rs`, wired today to `CLAUDE.md` alone. It carries what lies between `<!-- user:start -->` and `<!-- user:end -->`, and it returns the regenerated file unchanged when the existing file has no such block.

## What is built

- **One template** under `lib/templates/`, rendered through the token expander (`intentsvcs::rootfiles::substitute`): a title and one opening paragraph that say what the file is, the declared profiles, the roster table with each seat's moniker, name, role, who drives it and remit, the route to hv, and the verb that prints the terms. The roster table arrives as one token filled from the store, so the expander needs no new block kind. Its columns are padded to their widest cell, as the project's formatter pads a table, so a formatter run over the tree changes nothing in the generated part and is never its second writer. Each seat's driver comes from the board's declared human seat (WP-03), and a seat with no remit of its own shows its profile's default, read at the render and marked as the default. The route to hv is the profile's own section (WP-02), printed whole, and it names the mediator as the one reader of hv's inbox.
- **The preserved block.** The template ends on a block between `<!-- user:start -->` and `<!-- user:end -->`, the pair `carry_user_block` carries, and the project's own prose lives inside it. The function is reused, not copied. The README does not take the branch that guards `CLAUDE.md`, which holds back a file that carries no generated footer: a first render meets exactly such a file and must go on.
- **The first render.** A first render is one over a README that Intent has never rendered. The render's own record says so, and the presence of a block does not: each render records, in the declaration's canon file (WP-03), the sha256 of the README's text outside the block as it rendered it, and a README with no such record has never been rendered. It first places the whole existing file inside the block and then carries it, and the verb says so. A plain reuse of the function would lose every hand-written line, since it carries nothing when the existing file has no block. No hand-written line is lost, and the project prunes what the generated part now says. One exception, found on 2026-11-10 in the first swarm set up by hand in this thread's form: 5 of the 32 live READMEs open with a verblock, and a frontmatter block carried into the block would sit in the middle of the file. A generated view carries no verblock, so the first render does not carry a frontmatter block that opens the existing file: it drops it and names it on its own line of the report.
- **A remit written by hand.** No board has a stored remit today, and 26 state their seats' remits in README prose. A first render that filled every remit from the profile would state each seat's remit twice and differently, the default in the generated part and the project's own inside the block. So a seat whose remit was never set shows the profile's default marked as the default, and the sweep sets each board's own remits in the same step as its apply (WP-11).
- **Skew.** A hand edit outside the block is skew that `intent doctor` reports. An apply refuses to render over it, before anything is written, and names the lines and the remedy, which is to move them into the block: restoring the file would delete what someone wrote, and this package's promise is that a project loses none of it. A README that is only out of date, because a newer Intent renders it differently, re-renders. A render compared with the file cannot tell the two apart, and the recorded hash can: text outside the block that no longer matches the hash is an edit, and text that matches the hash but not this build's render is only out of date. The file index cannot stand in for the record, which cc measured on 2026-11-10: it lists every file a scan saw, whoever wrote it, so a hand-written README is already in it; every scan rebuilds it, so an edit is its baseline one scan later; and it lives in one machine's store and never reaches a clone. The record travels with the declaration, so a clone answers as the machine that rendered the README does.
- **The markers.** The block runs from the first start marker to the first end marker after it. A stray marker would therefore move the block's end and drop what follows it, and a README that only mentions the two markers would read as holding a block. So a render refuses, naming the line, a README whose markers are anything but one start followed by one end, and a first render refuses one that holds either marker at all.
- **Nothing guessed.** Every generated line has a declared source, the profile or the store. This is the lesson of issue 0672, where a template wrote a language's default build lines into a contract and was wrong in most of the fleet. AC-07.4 states it as a test.
- **No run state.** The roster table says nothing about whether a seat has run. The file is committed, and a seat's first pickup does not render it, so a mark there would be stale from that pickup on. The pickup is where run state is printed (WP-06).

## What the hand form showed

On 2026-11-10 Intent's own README was written by hand in this package's form (d09791705). cc read it as this package's builder, and vc took its findings under hv's pen.

- Its title and its opening paragraph, which give the history of the threads that built the whiteboard, sit where the generated part will go. The generated part has a title and an opening of its own. The history moves inside the block with the rest of the project's prose, because nothing in the profiles or the store declares it (AC-07.4).
- It names the one reader of hv's inbox. After WP-05 that reader is the mediator, so the generated route says so.
- It has no block, so it is a control for the first render: every line of it must come through inside the block.

## What it is not

It is not where a session learns its seat: WP-06 is. It is not issue 0672's fix, which changes `lib/templates/llm/_AGENTS.md` and is ruled separately.

## Rulings since this package was written, 2026-11-10

These are vc's rulings under the pen, made on ic's read of the dispatch rows and cc's read as builder, and written here once hv ratified the terms. Where one disagrees with the text above, it stands and the text above gives way.

A hand edit outside the block is a new doctor class, `roster-readme-edited`: shown, never counted, naming the lines and the remedy. The hard stop stays at `wb init --apply`. Out-of-date is `StaleRender`, with an arm proving it is never counted. The dropped verblock is a `note:`.

## Rulings on the second row read, 2026-11-10

These are vc's rulings under the pen on ic's read of this package against the dispatch table at d6f56d7e6. Where one disagrees with anything above, the section before it included, it stands and the text above gives way.

Out-of-date is NOT `StaleRender`, which the section above said. It is a class of its own, `roster-readme-behind`, with the remedy "`intent wb init --apply` re-renders it; only text the renderer owns differs". StaleRender's remedy names `intent sync`, which is the wrong verb for a file whose only renderer is `wb init --apply`, and `RootFileBehind` is about a root file canon writes. ## Builder and judge

So the shape in use is the one nothing describes, and each wearer has learned it from hv's prose and from what its predecessor left.

## What is built

- **One source for the duties.** What a controller does (take control, arm the watch, judge an ask against the lanes and the estate view, grant, deny, revoke, hold, release) moves to one template file. The dedicated coordinator's `AGENTS.md` and the hat's brief are both rendered from it, so the two shapes cannot drift.
- **Who may take it.** `intent estate control take` from a Claude session bound to a whiteboard node is refused unless that node is its board's vc, and the remedy says who may. `--hv "<words>"` overrides on hv's quoted word and records it, as it does today for a take under another name. - **The wearer's brief.** While a node's session holds control, its pickup prints that it wears the desk, the duties, and the asks waiting. The prompt hook already names waiting asks to a controller.
- **The board shows it.** The wearer's board header and `intent wb status` show the hat. It is read from the estate's control record at render time and stored nowhere else, so there is no second record to go stale.

The lanes, the slots and their verbs, and the dedicated coordinator `intent estate init` renders, which stays the other legal shape.

vc directs this package and judges each project's commit. There is no single builder: each board is converged by whoever the route below names, and vc claims nothing.

## The population

32 live boards on rhadamanth, measured on 2026-11-10: 18 under `~/Devel/prj`, 3 under `prj/Arca`, 9 in a client tree and 2 under `~/Devel/writing`. Backups, archives and vendored `deps/` copies are not boards. The census is re-run on the day, because the count is a reading and not a constant.

## The route, on hv's ruling of 2026-11-10

- **Intent's own board first.** `ac` was registered and `dc`'s role corrected from worker to devx by hand on 2026-11-10 (d09791705), on hv's word, so the apply reads both as unchanged. What is left is the hand form's retirement. And vc asks hv to retire directive 2, the brief written by hand, which leaves hv's board only on hv's word.
- **A project with no running session** is converged from vc's session: the dry run is read, `intent wb init --apply` is run, and one commit carries exactly what the verb printed.
- **A project whose vc or sc is running** is converged by that node. It is sent the exact step, runs it inside its own chain, and reports its sha, which vc reads. This is the rule since the Gtools release hold of 2026-09-25: only that node knows its project's holds.

## Before any write

- The brew-installed Intent on this machine carries WP-02 to WP-10.
- vc has measured what the released Intent before this thread does with a board at the new schema, and every machine that reads a project's board runs an Intent that can read it before that project is converged.

- On each board, the mediator has surfaced the live messages addressed to hv and cleared them, so the apply is not refused (AC-05.6).

- **Pipeliner's `sc`.** hv, 2026-11-10: "I think that was a mistake and probably needs to be revoked and just back to a normal VC/CC/IC/DC/AC mix." It reverses rulings 9 and 10 of the writing-estate plan of 2026-11-05, so it is confirmed with hv and put to Pipeliner's own nodes before any write. It installs Intent nowhere and makes a board in no project that has none (hv, 2026-09-23). It pushes nothing. It writes nothing in a project but what `intent wb init --apply` printed.

Molt's guide `docs/guides/sleeve-agents.md` and its roster README record the project suffixes hv named on 2026-10-21. They come to cite Intent's terms and record the suffixes nowhere, by molt-vc's hand.
